subject: science
domain: From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes
intro: Multicellular organisms are organized in a hierarchy, from small to large: cells form tissues, tissues form organs, organs form organ systems, and organ systems work together to make the whole organism. Each level has specific functions, and the levels interact. For example, muscle cells form muscle tissue, which forms the heart (an organ), which is part of the circulatory system, which works with other systems to keep the organism alive. A model showing these levels helps illustrate how the parts interact to carry out life functions.

items.prompt: Put these in order from smallest to largest: organ, cell, organ system, tissue. Explain the hierarchy.

steps: The smallest unit is the cell.
Cells of the same type form a tissue, and tissues form an organ.
Organs working together form an organ system, so the order is cell, tissue, organ, organ system.
solution.answer: Cell, tissue, organ, organ system: cells form tissues, tissues form organs, organs form systems.

items.prompt: Muscle cells form heart muscle tissue, which forms the heart, part of the circulatory system. Identify each level in this example.

steps: The muscle cell is the cell level.
Heart muscle tissue is the tissue level, and the heart is the organ level.
The circulatory system is the organ system level, showing all four levels.
solution.answer: Cell = muscle cell, tissue = heart muscle, organ = heart, organ system = circulatory system.

items.prompt: How do the digestive and circulatory systems interact to nourish the body?

steps: The digestive system breaks food into nutrients the body can absorb.
The circulatory system carries those nutrients in the blood to all the cells.
So the two systems interact: digestion provides nutrients and circulation delivers them.
solution.answer: The digestive system provides nutrients and the circulatory system delivers them to cells, so the systems interact.

items.prompt: What is the smallest level in the organization of a multicellular organism?

steps: The hierarchy goes from small to large.
The smallest level is the cell.

items.prompt: A tissue is a group of similar cells doing a job. Give an example of a tissue and the organ it helps form.

steps: A tissue is made of similar cells with a shared function.
Muscle tissue is made of muscle cells and helps form organs like the heart.
So muscle tissue is an example, and it helps form the heart.
solution.answer: Muscle tissue (made of muscle cells) helps form an organ such as the heart.

items.prompt: Use the hierarchy to explain how a single level failing, such as a damaged organ, can affect the whole organism.

steps: Organs are part of organ systems that keep the organism alive.
If an organ like the heart is damaged, the circulatory system cannot deliver blood well.
Because the systems interact to support the organism, a failure at one level can harm the whole organism.
solution.answer: A damaged organ weakens its system, and since the systems interact to keep the organism alive, the whole organism is affected.
